chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Muawiya ibn Wahb, from his father, who said:

We ate in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So when the meal was raised, he picked up what had fallen from it and ate it. Then he said to us: 'It negates poverty and increases children.'

key_terms.الْخِوَان: The dining spread or cloth on which food is placed

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and practical benefit of picking up and eating food that falls from the table?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the virtue of frugality by consuming dropped food, linking it to divine blessings of wealth and progeny. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on avoiding israf (wastefulness) as a means of attracting barakah, a concept deeply rooted in both Prophetic tradition and Shia jurisprudence regarding daily conduct.
